title: An experiment for our schools - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Cowen quotes reporting that at least nine US schools across Florida, Georgia and Colorado will install teacher-activated nonlethal drones from Austin-based Mithril Defense that can reach an active shooter in 15 seconds, and draws the investment conclusion: be long countries where local crime is a major problem.

insights.claim: At least nine US schools -- three in Florida, five in Georgia and one in Colorado -- will this year house storage boxes containing teacher-activated nonlethal drones that can fly through halls and smash windows to reach an active shooter.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A first commercial deployment footprint in K-12 buildings marks the moment counter-personnel drones cross from military into routine civilian institutional procurement.
insights.quote: At least nine schools — three in Florida, five in Georgia and one in Colorado — will have storage boxes that house the plastic, nonlethal aircraft made by Austin-based Mithril Defense.

insights.claim: Austin-based Mithril Defense builds plastic nonlethal aircraft that reach a shooter within 15 seconds of teacher activation and subdue targets with strobes, sirens, pepper gel, or ramming at 60 mph.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A named private vendor with a 15-second response spec and nonlethal payloads defines the emerging product category for indoor autonomous security response.
insights.quote: The aircraft are designed to distract their targets by flashing strobes, blaring sirens, spraying them with pepper gel, or ramming into them at 60 mph.
insights.locator: The aircraft are designed to distract

themes.theme: Crime as an investable macro variable

insights.claim: Cowen repeats a standing recommendation to be long countries where local crime is a major problem, on the logic that severe crime generates large and growing demand for security technology and protective products.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Treats high-crime jurisdictions as structural demand pools for defense-tech and security vendors rather than as pure discounts to equity risk premia.
insights.quote: be long countries where local crime is a major problem.

insights.claim: School districts are willing to pre-position robotic force-response hardware rather than rely solely on human response, indicating institutional buyers will pay for automated physical security where response latency is the binding constraint.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Latency-driven procurement opens a recurring hardware-plus-service budget line in public education, a large and politically insulated buyer.
insights.locator: Schools in at least three states will be equipped
